claims.claim: Schrödinger signed a strategic software collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb to deploy Bunsen, its agentic AI co-scientist, inside BMS research workflows.

Schrödinger co-founded Tectora Therapeutics, contributed two early-stage programs, retained an equity stake plus milestone/royalty eligibility, and Tectora raised a $55M Series A from NEA and RA Capital.

factors.name: enterprise agentic-AI adoption
factors.basis: BMS deployment is external validation of Bunsen within a major pharma R&D organization.

factors.name: asset monetization model
factors.basis: Tectora converts internal programs into equity, milestones, royalties and platform usage while external capital funds development.

risks.risk: Strategic collaborations validate interest but do not establish the magnitude or durability of software revenue or drug-program success.

unknowns.unknown: Commercial economics of the BMS Bunsen agreement were not disclosed in the cited release.

claims.claim: The BMS agreement expands an existing relationship from computational software toward agentic discovery workflows, providing a concrete enterprise test of Schrödinger's newer AI layer.

The Tectora structure shifts two programs into a separately financed vehicle while preserving Schrödinger equity and downstream economics, creating a capital-sharing execution model rather than retaining all development burden internally.

factors.name: platform-to-workflow conversion
factors.basis: Bunsen is moving into a named large-pharma research organization.

factors.name: capital efficiency
factors.basis: External Series A capital supports contributed programs while Schrödinger retains contingent economics.

risks.risk: Partner adoption and financing structures can fail to translate into material recurring software growth or successful clinical assets.

unknowns.unknown: No current security valuation or probability-adjusted drug value is asserted by Scout.
